WHY IT WAS DESIGNED

FROM OBSERVER TO DECISION-MAKER

Political and security events often appear simpler from the outside. In practice, decisions involve incomplete information, competing priorities, institutional responsibilities and consequences that unfold over time.

This simulator places players in the decision-maker’s seat, using choices and branching consequences to reveal how complex decisions develop, how NATO structures interact and why collective action rarely follows a simple path.

WHO IT IS FOR

OPEN TO CURIOUS DECISION-MAKERS

No specialist background is required. The simulator is designed for students, educators, professionals, NATO enthusiasts and anyone curious about how political and security decisions develop under pressure.

CREATED BY

AN INDEPENDENT STUDENT PROJECT

Created by an International Relations student, the project combines public research, strategic analysis, scenario design and front-end development. Selected insights from a NATO internship are included only where publicly available or safely generalised.
